grade_definitions.V: Black-box verifiable by canonical conformance vectors and fixture runner results.
grade_definitions.A: Verifiable by the public SDK API shape and inventory; no implementation-private inspection is required.
grade_definitions.U: Verifiable only by implementation, configuration, or data-flow audit evidence.

sdk_conformance_contract.evidence_coverage_semantics_note: A clause's required_evidence enumerates the ACCEPTABLE evidence kinds for that clause (acceptable-set semantics), not a mandate that every listed kind be present. For a clause claim with result=pass or result=fail: at least one evidence entry MUST be present (already required by the schema when result != not_applicable), and every evidence[].kind MUST be a member of that clause's required_evidence set in this contract. Evidence whose kind falls outside the clause's required_evidence set MUST NOT be accepted as substantiation for that clause. result=not_applicable is exempt from evidence-kind coverage but MUST carry a machine-readable rationale.
rules: Each SDK release claiming Arkret v1 conformance MUST publish one claim object against this exact contract digest.
The claim MUST bind the exact SDK artifact digest and spec revision, and MUST carry an issuer signature over the domain-separated RFC 8785 JCS claim bytes with proof omitted.
Every evidence reference MUST carry a non-zero immutable content digest; consumers MUST verify all digests and the issuer verification method before accepting the claim.
Every applicable clause MUST appear exactly once; not_applicable MUST include a machine-readable rationale.
Evidence references MUST be content-addressed or carry an immutable CI run identifier.

A verifier MUST enforce evidence_coverage_semantics: for every clause claim whose result is pass or fail, it MUST reject the claim unless at least one evidence entry is present and every evidence[].kind is a member of that clause's required_evidence set. A pass/fail clause substantiated only by evidence kinds outside its required_evidence set MUST be rejected. This check is independent of, and applied in addition to, the digest and signature checks above.
Section numbers and table row numbers are not clause identifiers; only clause_id is stable.

clauses.summary: Validate Event Envelope and payload class before consumption
Do not expose a bypass for proof, HLC, actor sequence, prev refs, or authorization refs
Do not expose configuration that disables authorization constraints
Fail closed for causal, revoked, and invalid-proof states
Model cursor values as opaque and expose no structured decode API
Reject malformed or non-canonical JSON without repair
Reject malformed HLC without normalization or truncation
Preserve prev refs, authorization refs, and actor sequence constraints during retry
Verify governance binding and KeyPackage DID before decrypting or encrypting
Do not disclose plaintext or keys to unauthorized services
Light clients must not authorize a DataEvent from a single leaf proof
Apply late-key-recovery visibility checks before decrypting
Fail closed on unknown critical features or unmet requirements
Reject production use of test DIDs, keys, and trust domains
Reconcile trimmed build capabilities with every published profile claim
Preserve unknown values from open registries without failing whole-object deserialization
Preserve explicit extension-slot content through canonical round trips and forwarding
Model ack_token as opaque and expose no structured decode API
Do not automatically replay retry_safe=false operations and rotate the request key when content changes
Honor Retry-After without clamping it into an earlier retry
Continue pagination only when has_more is true
Expose the canonical confusable check as a callable SDK utility

tier_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.
tier_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
tier_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks implementation profiles outside the v1 minimal interop floor, including evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA) and opt-in product/privacy features such as productivity, disappearing messages, calendar events, pins, and search. Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely; implementations MUST claim only entries they actually support. When an underlying external standard matures, a replacement profile with stable version pinning can supersede that entry.

profile_tiers.test_build_stance_rule: Test/conformance builds are marked solely by the canonical development_mode=true flag on the ServiceDescribe (see zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.1.2 and zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.0), which gates the test-only /_arkret/_conformance/* debug namespace and forces verified_profiles=[]. There is no separate ak.profile.* test-build profile: a test build is a deployment stance, not a negotiated interop capability.

candidate_profiles_tier_rule: Profiles pairing unregistered candidate workflow concept/action names / capabilities with an explicit fail-closed gate. Receivers MUST treat any capability action whose `profile` points to a candidate profile as unknown (risk_tier=high default) unless they implement the profile. Candidate profiles are NOT part of v1 active conformance and SHOULD be promoted (with paired wire Event.kind values registered under `ak.*`) once their underlying surface is formally registered.
profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1.description: Fail-closed Realm role profile for the canonical two-principal Direct Conversation Collaboration Realm. The role is identified only by schema_refs containing this profile together with fields.collaboration_role=direct_conversation.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: not applicable: a receiver that cannot enforce this role MUST reject or quarantine the Realm create as unsupported_feature and MUST NOT treat it as an ordinary Collaboration Realm

binding_invariants: schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and fields.collaboration_role MUST equal direct_conversation; either marker without the other is schema_violation.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both equal e2ee_required.

The ak.realm.create Event requirements.schema MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and requirements.critical_extensions MUST contain fail_closed=true id ak.feature.direct_conversation_realm_role.v1 for payload scope.
Exactly the two stable subject DIDs in the canonical active binding may be active Realm principal members; any third-party join or invite MUST be rejected.
Space events are forbidden in a Direct Conversation Realm with direct_conversation_space_forbidden; additional ordinary Strands remain allowed.
The canonical main Strand MUST be active, belong to the Realm, have no Circle scope, and expose an active primary discussion track.

Cross-Principal-Server creation MUST complete the participant-authorized peer KeyPackage claim authoring step before the binding authoring step; Direct Conversation claims MUST bind pair_key, intended Realm, main Strand and MLS group and MUST NOT use a last-resort KeyPackage.

A participant leave or ban, Realm tombstone or destroy, or main Strand archive or tombstone retires the active binding and requires a fresh Realm, main Strand and MLS group for the next create=true resolution.

Contact tombstone and direct_message consent revoke block new resolver success and default message send but do not by themselves rewrite Realm history or retire an otherwise structurally active binding.

ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.description: Realm profile for a principal-scoped durable control stream (the Principal Control Realm role; see zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7). It is an ordinary Collaboration Realm at the envelope level, but reducers MUST treat fields.purpose=principal_control + this schema_ref as an allowlist-bound control stream, not as a user collaboration space.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Receivers that do not understand ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 MUST treat the Realm as an ordinary Collaboration Realm and MUST NOT accept device/session/cross-signing state from it as principal control state.

rules: Agent PCR events MUST target the Agent DID bound to the Realm; controller execution uses actor_id=Agent DID, executed_by=controller DID, and a verified authorization_ref.
Controller-owned accountability and selector facts MUST target the controller PCR and reference the Agent DID; they MUST NOT be moved into the Agent PCR.
Pairing requests and account approval notifications MUST NOT be written to any PCR or Collaboration Realm.

binding_invariants: realm_id MUST equal the principal_control_realm_id resolved for the principal DID.
fields.purpose MUST be principal_control and schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.
encryption_profile MUST be mls_rfc9420; PCRs MUST NOT use none or external.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both be e2ee_required; a PCR genesis declaring either floor below e2ee_required MUST be rejected (no plaintext-floor PCR exists in v1).

history_visibility MUST be restricted; new same-principal devices obtain prior control history via durable device-list / normalized principal view baseline and policy-gated MLS history key share, not by joining at the current epoch.
Control events MUST bind principal_id / device_id / session grant audience to the same principal DID or an explicitly trusted recovery/session issuer.

A managed Agent principal_control_realm_id and immutable requested_scope commitment MUST be verified from the unique ArkretPrincipalControlRealm DID service entry at accepted-at; the public entry fixes only realm_id, controller_did, authorization_ref and the domain-separated requested_scope_digest. The complete scope MUST come from a controller-signed verifier/audience/challenge-bound private disclosure whose digest matches that commitment. Implementation-private deterministic derivation or a service-local Agent row is not protocol evidence.
Managed Agent PCR genesis created_by and notary MUST equal the Agent DID; a controller authoring under delegation MUST be recorded as executed_by and MUST NOT synthesize an Agent signature.

ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.description: Degraded E2EE profile. Allows `mls_send_pause="advisory"` (cf. §2.4.1) so that low-latency interactive scenarios (real-time AV, collaborative editing, in-game chat) do not block message send on MLS commit completion. Cost: removed members can continue decrypting a small window of subsequent messages. NOT for general chat / collaboration / compliance use. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 MUST reject Realm create / ak.realm.policy_components writes that set mls_send_pause="advisory" (reason: profile_unsupported / mls_send_pause_advisory_requires_e2ee_relaxed_profile). They MUST NOT silently accept the advisory string without honoring the relaxed semantics.

downgrade_declaration_obligation.policy_declaration_required: Realm create or ak.realm.policy_components MUST explicitly declare ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 before mls_send_pause="advisory" is accepted. Out-of-band deployment config, UI-only labels, or a missing governance_binding GroupContext extension MUST NOT be treated as a valid downgrade declaration.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.service_describe_required: The serving implementation MUST advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 and the claimed profile in ServiceDescribe before accepting advisory writes or projecting the Realm as relaxed to a peer/facade.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.binding_profile_required: Every MLS governance_binding emitted for a relaxed Realm MUST carry binding_profile="ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1" and the negotiated reducer_profile. Missing binding_profile, binding_profile="ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1", or an unsupported profile id is a fail-closed mismatch.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.export_marker_required: Sync metadata, snapshots, backups, exports, and interop mapping receipts that summarize the Realm MUST preserve e2ee_relaxed=true and relaxed_window_max_ms. Consumers that observe advisory semantics without this marker MUST assume the downgrade is undeclared and reject new old-epoch decrypt admission.

client_ui_requirements.banner_warning: Realms declaring this profile MUST display a banner-level warning indicating that kick / ban is not cryptographically immediate; the warning MAY be temporarily collapsed but MUST NOT be permanently dismissable.
client_ui_requirements.invite_warning: When a user invites a new member, the UI SHOULD prompt with 'this Realm uses degraded E2EE' so the invitee can make an informed decision.
client_ui_requirements.export_marker: Sync metadata / backup / export MUST preserve a `e2ee_relaxed=true` marker so downstream consumers know the cryptographic guarantee is relaxed.

downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `ak.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.
downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment with active Audit Applet Binding) MUST NOT enable ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.

restricted_requires: each federation peer describes a fanout SLA not exceeding the relaxed window
each federation peer explicitly advertises ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 when it is expected to accept relaxed old-epoch decrypt admission
federation_guard.interop_floor: Full MLS governance binding (ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1) remains the federation E2EE interoperability floor. The relaxed profile (ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1) is a declared downgrade below that floor and is accepted across federation only for restricted/closed deployments that satisfy the bounded-SLA requirements above.

fail_closed_conditions: combination of ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 with ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1, compliance-tier E2EE, active Audit Applet Binding, federation_policy=open, or federation_policy=quarantine
restricted federation without peer fanout SLA bounds within relaxed_window_max_ms
governance_binding.binding_profile missing, unsupported, or inconsistent with the Realm downgrade declaration
receiver old-epoch decrypt gap exceeds relaxed_window_max_ms or the absolute hard ceiling of 300000 ms
ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.compliance_unfit: Compliance / regulatory contexts that require 'kick-out is immediately effective' MUST NOT use this profile. Use non-E2EE Realm (encryption_profile="none") + enclave channels instead. Spec deliberately does not allow further relaxation than this profile; deployments needing more leniency are out of v1 E2EE scope.

additional_requirements.invite_claim_reducer_authority_must: ak.invite.claim MUST be decided by the destination Realm reducer, not by Auth Server, verification service, Sync Service ingress, or client projection caches.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_token_commitment_must: Reducer MUST match payload.token_commitment to the pending ak.invite.third_party invite and reject mismatch or already-claimed commitments with no membership proposal.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_allowlist_recheck_must: Reducer MUST re-check binding_proof.verification_service_id against the current effective Realm allowlist and any invite-pinned service DID before accepting subject_proof.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_nonce_dedup_must: Reducer MUST treat (invite_id, claim_nonce) and token_commitment as one-time constraints and reject replay with duplicate_conflict.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_membership_conversion_must: Successful claim MUST atomically transition invite pending -> claimed and materialize only a subject-bound standard invite or membership proposal; final join still requires ak.invite.accept or an explicitly profiled equivalent path.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_expiry_cleanup_must: Reducer MUST expire third-party invites before claim acceptance when expires_at <= now and trigger token material cleanup obligations from third-party-invites.md §6.1.

e2ee_mls_interop_floor.applies_when: Any federation transaction carries or depends on encryption_profile="mls_rfc9420", ak.mls.genesis, ak.mls.commit, ak.mls.welcome, MLS-backed E2EE DataEvents, or covered_seals_cell state.
e2ee_mls_interop_floor.downgrade_admission: Only closed or restricted federation may accept ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1, and restricted federation MUST satisfy the bounded-SLA federation_guard in that profile. Open and quarantine federation MUST reject the relaxed downgrade.
e2ee_mls_interop_floor.fail_closed_behavior: A receiver that cannot verify the minimum profile, sees a missing/inconsistent binding_profile or reducer_profile, or cannot prove the relaxed federation guard MUST reject or quarantine the affected MLS artifact/DataEvent before advancing Realm frontier.

ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1.description: High-assurance / sovereign / regulated / multi-writer federation profile. Adds mandatory proactive frontier exchange with fail-state semantics on top of the ak.profile.federation_minimal.v1 baseline. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.3 and zh/sync/sovereign-deployment.md §11.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: reject claim of ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1 if proactive frontier exchange or stale_peer fail-state is not implemented

additional_requirements.frontier_probe_capability_must: Peer MUST expose capability-gated frontier probe endpoint per federation.md §4.5.1.
additional_requirements.proactive_exchange_must: Per federation-visible Realm, per authorized peer, frontier probe interval MUST be <= 3600 seconds.
additional_requirements.fail_state_must: Three consecutive probe failures (peer unreachable or signature failure) MUST mark the peer as 'stale_peer' for that Realm. Separately, an aggregate-commitment difference MUST first be reduced via per-actor challenge/backfill on the intersection of replicated actors, comparing each (realm_id, actor_id, actor_seq) as a canonical sibling SET of (event_id,event_digest,prev_frontier_digest), not as a single hash. Different event_id/hash siblings at one actor_seq are legal within the event-and-patch.md §2.6 limits and MUST converge by validated set union. A same-event_id/different-digest conflict, an over-limit sibling set, a profile-declared non-joinable sibling conflict, or inconsistent witness payloads for the same complete attestation scope MUST quarantine the affected increments on the FIRST confirmed occurrence and MUST NOT be folded into the three-consecutive-failure window. Raw frontier_root/heads/range-root differences across different scopes, and incomplete subsets of a legal sibling set, MUST NOT alone count as probe failure or witness_disagreement.
additional_requirements.stale_peer_behavior_must: While a peer is in 'stale_peer' state: MUST quarantine its push payloads for the affected evidence scope (no local frontier advancement from that scope); MUST surface state via operator alarm channel; MAY refuse to fanout new Events to that peer. Stale status MUST clear after the original evidence is resolved: the disputed event id/digest or over-fork/non-joinable sibling bucket has an authorized canonical resolution and the peer matches that canonical sibling set, or witnesses for the same complete attestation scope again sign one consistent payload. Scope-different peers MUST NOT be required to have globally identical heads.

ak.profile.auth_server.v1.description: Arkret v1 Auth Server profile. Auth Servers verify login factors (password / passkey / OIDC / SSO / recovery), issue short-lived audience-bound `ak.session.grant` artefacts, expose session-grant introspection / revocation, and MAY surface a `ak.self.policy.query.check` decision endpoint. Auth Servers are NOT canonical identity registries (DID documents / key logs live in `ak.profile.identity_registry.v1`) and are NOT principal servers (no Realm-authoritative event acceptance). Coauth is the reference implementation. See zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md, zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5, zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §9a.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit optional operation or return unsupported_feature

additional_requirements.session_grant_must_be_short_lived: Auth Server MUST cap session_grant TTL well below the Realm policy review horizon (per device-lifecycle.md §5, typical ceiling is minutes-to-hours, not days).
additional_requirements.audience_binding_must: Every issued session_grant MUST carry an `audience` claim; auth servers MUST refuse to issue grants for audiences they have not been configured to serve.
additional_requirements.session_grant_release_readiness_must: Release readiness MUST cover ak.vector.auth.session_grant_audience_binding.v1 and ak.vector.auth.soft_logout_did_proof.v1: proof binds challenge, audience, request_canonical_digest, principal and device; stranger audiences are rejected; soft_logged_out recovery requires fresh DID proof; development_mode=true never advertises verified profiles.
additional_requirements.not_identity_registry_must: Auth Server MUST NOT claim `ak.profile.identity_registry.v1`; any DID document / key-log surface it exposes MUST be declared on `compat_surfaces[]` as `delegated_resolver` rather than self-claimed canonical authority.
additional_requirements.not_principal_server_must: Auth Server MUST NOT claim `ak.profile.principal_server.v1`; Realm event acceptance is the principal server role and is incompatible with auth-server-only deployments.
additional_requirements.verified_profiles_dev_mode_must: When `development_mode=true`, `verified_profiles[]` MUST be `[]` per sync/service-surface.md §3.0; cotest writes verified entries only after a passing verified-profile suite run.

ak.profile.push_gateway.v1.description: Push gateway base profile. Provides the device registration / notify operation surface. All implementations claiming this profile MUST also implement ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (default interop privacy baseline) — see zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §5.1. Visible-payload variants are opt-in only via ak.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: strip unsupported plaintext fields

ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1.description: Default push gateway privacy baseline. Every implementation claiming ak.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile. Provider-facing payloads MUST NOT carry stable identifying fields (principal DID, sender DID, Realm id / name / avatar, Strand id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction value, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key). Payloads MUST be restricted to per-(recipient_service_id, principal, device, push_route) pairwise pseudonym push_target_id + closed-enum wakeup hint fields (wakeup_kind, badge_count, unread_increment, l10n_key). See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §4.5 / §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5a.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: MUST fail closed; gateways unable to enforce blind wakeup MUST NOT claim ak.profile.push_gateway.v1

additional_requirements.stable_identifier_ban_must: Provider payload MUST NOT contain principal DID, sender DID / handle, Realm id / name, Strand id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction emoji, attachment filename, IP, geolocation, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key.
additional_requirements.pseudonym_scope_must: push_target_id MUST be a pairwise pseudonym scoped to (recipient_service_id, principal, device, push_route); MUST NOT be reusable across Principal Server contexts.
additional_requirements.default_claim_must: Any implementation claiming ak.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile and MUST NOT advertise downgrade switches that disable blind wakeup.

ak.profile.push_gateway.visible_notifica.description: Opt-in push gateway profile for deployments that require visible notification fields (e.g. titles, sender labels) in provider payloads. Claiming this profile is permitted ONLY when (1) Realm policy explicitly lists the gateway in plaintext_visible_services AND declares visible_notification allowance, (2) per-device opt-in is recorded in ak.device authorization state, and (3) the client UI clearly surfaces that visible-notification mode is active. Even when claimed, payloads MUST stay minimised: no message body, no DID URL, no cross-Realm stable correlation key, no IP / geolocation, no free-form text outside the profile-declared field set. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; deployments that cannot guarantee Realm policy + device opt-in + UI disclosure MUST NOT claim this profile

additional_requirements.policy_gate_must: Realm policy MUST list the gateway service DID in plaintext_visible_services with visible_notification explicitly allowed.
additional_requirements.device_opt_in_must: Each receiving device MUST record an opt-in flag in its authorization state; absent opt-in, sender / Realm service MUST fall back to blind wakeup.
additional_requirements.ui_disclosure_must: Client UI MUST clearly indicate visible notification is active to the user.
additional_requirements.payload_minimisation_must: Even when claimed, payload MUST NOT carry message body, DID URLs, cross-Realm stable correlation keys, IP / geolocation, or untyped free-form text.

ak.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrou.description: Interop compatibility profile for Matrix push gateway passthrough. Implementations claiming this profile MAY accept Matrix-shaped push gateway payloads as an external interop bridge to Matrix push gateways but MUST NOT mix this profile with ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 on the same notify path: the Matrix push gateway shape carries identifying fields incompatible with the default Arkret privacy baseline. Bridges MUST partition traffic so that any peer or device negotiated under ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (i.e. the default v1 baseline) NEVER receives a matrix_passthrough payload. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1 and zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §11.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; bridges that cannot partition traffic MUST NOT claim this profile

additional_requirements.partition_must: Bridges MUST partition push traffic so that Arkret v1 default-baseline peers (ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1) NEVER receive matrix_passthrough-shaped payloads.
additional_requirements.no_default_mixing_must: Implementations MUST NOT advertise both ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 and ak.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrough.v1 as applying to the same (recipient_service_id, device) tuple.
additional_requirements.interop_only_must: This profile is interop-only; it MUST NOT be used as a substitute for ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 in default Arkret deployments.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: return unsupported_feature

additional_requirements.transaction_push_per_delivery_signature_: ak.edge.applet.command.transaction MUST require a per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature in both node->Applet and app/bridge->arkret inbound directions; pure bearer-only transaction push MUST be rejected with http_signature_required.
additional_requirements.transaction_push_covered_components_must: Signature-Input covered components MUST include @method, @target-uri, @authority, content-digest, source-service-id, destination-service-id and idempotency-key; created/expires MUST satisfy the federation.md section 3.2 replay window.
additional_requirements.transaction_push_source_anchor_must: Receivers MUST persist a source_signature_anchor audit value bound to operation_id, direction, source_service_id, destination_service_id, verification_method/keyid, registration_epoch or source key-state evidence, Idempotency-Key, Content-Digest, covered components, created and expires.

Account-aggregate sync is NOT covered: Arkret v1 chose a streaming push form (ak.self.account.stream.subscribe / GET /account/subscribe with NDJSON frames) over Matrix's long-poll /sync, so wire-shape parity is not claimed for this surface — Matrix clients MUST adapt the account-aggregate consumption loop. ak.profile.circle_seal_cadence.fixed_5m..description: Named cadence profile for confidential Circle sub-seal commitments. Implementations claiming this profile MUST emit ak.circle.seal_commit on a fixed time cadence (5 minutes, max jitter 30 seconds), MUST include empty-batch commitments, and MUST NOT use event-count or activity-triggered public commitments. Mobile energy saving may batch private sub-seal upload, but MUST NOT relax the public Realm seal cadence.

period_ms.rationale: Public Realm seal commitment cadence is fixed at 5 minutes for this profile.

max_jitter_ms.rationale: Bounded scheduling jitter; implementations MUST NOT encode activity by delaying beyond this window.

empty_batch_commitments.rationale: No-activity intervals still emit commitments to avoid leaking activity frequency.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; confidential Circle deployments MUST NOT claim an event-count cadence as equivalent

ak.profile.cross_signing.reset.v1.description: Hardening profile for high-risk cross-signing reset. Claimants MUST accept ak.cross_signing.reset only with one valid reset proof family, enforce generation monotonicity, clock skew, and replay rejection, and require a successor ak.cross_signing.publish within the recovery window. Verification rules and reason codes are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

max_clock_skew_seconds.rationale: Maximum allowed deviation between `ak.cross_signing.reset.issued_at` and receiver local clock. Default 300s mirrors policy-decision freshness windows; receivers MAY tighten down to 60s for high-assurance deployments or relax up to 900s for federated peers with documented clock skew. Beyond the configured value receivers MUST emit cross_signing_reset_clock_skew_exceeded.

publish_recovery_window_seconds.rationale: Maximum interval after an accepted reset within which the successor ak.cross_signing.publish MUST be observed; receivers MUST otherwise enter the 'no usable SSK/USK' state from §14.2 step 5. Default 24h matches the §14.1 normative requirement.

reset_replay_cache_min_retention_seconds.rationale: Minimum retention for the (principal_id, previous_generation) replay-rejection cache used by §14.4 通用规则. MUST be at least `publish_recovery_window_seconds + 3600` so that no late-arriving duplicate reset can bypass the cache before the successor publish window closes. Default = 24h + 1h slack.

ak.profile.circle_conformance.v1.description: Conformance profile pinning the machine-contract surface for Circle (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary; see zh/models/circle.md). Splits actor submit-payload (scope_circle_id only) from canonical reducer-output (tagged effective_scope on Event envelope + materialized object), and pins the Circle event-kind family, member-state transition table, encryption-profile compatibility, and scope-rebind reducer-reject semantics. Required by implementations that emit or consume Circle events or that materialize Circle-scoped Strand / Message / Morph / Relation / Space objects.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: implementations that cannot enforce canonical reducer-stamped effective_scope MUST NOT claim ak.profile.circle_conformance.v1; receivers MUST treat any unknown Circle event-kind as schema_violation

additional_requirements.submit_payload_must: Submit payload for ak.strand.create / ak.message.create / ak.morph.create / ak.relation.create / ak.space.create / ak.space.parent MUST carry only scope_circle_id (id:circle | null). Reducer MUST reject any submit payload that also carries effective_scope (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).
additional_requirements.canonical_reducer_output_must: Reducer MUST stamp tagged effective_scope on accepted Event envelope and materialized object cell. effective_scope is immutable per-event; later scope_circle_id rebinds MUST NOT re-interpret historical events.
additional_requirements.scope_rebind_default_reject_must: Default reducer MUST reject scope_circle_id rebind (None<->Some, Some(A)->Some(B)) with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile-declared audit-paired rebind MAY be permitted, but MUST emit ak.audit.accessed pairing.
additional_requirements.circle_encryption_profile_floor_must: Circle.encryption_profile may be none or mls_rfc9420. Reducer MUST reject plaintext Circle creation or update when the parent Realm encryption_profile is mls_rfc9420 or the effective content_encryption_floor is e2ee_required (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor).
additional_requirements.circle_content_encryption_floor_must: Circle.content_encryption_floor (allow_plaintext | e2ee_required) is optional and symmetric with Circle.metadata_encryption_floor: when omitted it inherits the parent Realm content_encryption_floor, and the effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle content_encryption_floor). Reducer MUST reject a Circle floor below the effective floor and MUST reject content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required on an encryption_profile=none Circle (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor). See zh/models/circle.md §7.
additional_requirements.encryption_floor_ratchet_must: The effective content_encryption_floor and effective metadata encryption floor of any scope (Realm-default or Circle) are one-way ratchets: monotonically non-decreasing over time. A ak.realm.policy_components or ak.circle.update that lowers the effective content floor from e2ee_required to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected (reason=content_encryption_floor_downgrade); one that lowers the effective metadata floor MUST be rejected (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade). Tightening is always allowed. Vectors: ak.vector.e2ee.content_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.metadata_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.circle.content_floor_below_realm_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.in_place_enable.v1.
additional_requirements.circle_membership_subset_must: Circle.members MUST be a strict subset of parent Realm.members; reducer MUST reject ak.circle.member.state -> join when the target actor is not a `join` member of the parent Realm (reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member).
additional_requirements.scope_invariant_must: Sync Service MUST NOT deliver events with effective_scope.kind=circle to actors not in that Circle's member frontier at the event's causal frontier (see zh/models/circle.md §9.3 scope-delivery invariant).
